rationale: Decoded the rejected configuration entries by extending the rejection operand to include each ConfChangeV2's transition and change list, and the draft-side run answers the last open question about the mechanism. The log at the rejecting nodes is '1:t0 2:t2(tr=1,1:4) 3:t0 4:t2(tr=1,0:4)': index 2 is a joint-enter change that REMOVES node 4 (change type 1), index 4 is a joint-enter change that ADDS node 4 (change type 0), and neither is a leave-joint entry. So the committed history contains a joint configuration entered by a change that removes a non-member - a no-op change in terms of the voter set, since removing a node that is not present changes nothing - and then a second joint-enter change in the same configuration. The AutoLeave promise is what failed to break the cycle: appliedTo only proposes the leave when the applying node is the leader, so a joint change whose proposer is displaced before it applies the change leaves the cluster joint with nobody having proposed the leave, and the next leader's guard sees a non-joint tracker plus a stale pendingConfIndex and appends the second joint-enter change, which every node that applies the log in order then rejects. I request isolated execution so the decoded entries are receipt-backed before that account replaces the earlier, coarser explanation.

scope.description: Fifteenth revision of the same fixed harness; probes A-C, the deterministic joint-change case and the deterministic stale-guard case are unchanged. The sweep keeps configuration targets, application lag, joint transitions, restarts, the liveness witness and the recovered apply guard, and the rejection operand log_types now decodes each EntryConfChangeV2 in the observed range into its transition and change list, e.g. '2:t2(tr=1,1:4)' for a JointImplicit removal of node 4, alongside applied_before, applying_before, reapplied_entry and the node state. invariant_sweep_summary still reports all counters.
assumptions: Everything comes from the snapshot's own facilities (newTestRaft, newTestMemoryStorage, newNetwork, nextEnts, confChangeToMsg, applyConfChange, hasUnappliedConfChanges, promotable, newRaft, SetHardState, raftLog.slice, proto.Unmarshal); no production logic is modified.

log_types decodes the entries the rejecting node currently holds for [firstIndex, committed], capped at eight entries; it reports change type and node id per change, which is enough to tell a leave-joint entry (no changes) from a membership change.

The operands still do not show which node proposed each entry or whether the proposing leader was displaced before applying it, so the account of why no leave was appended is inferred from the source condition on appliedTo plus the decoded entries.
Randomness is fixed per seed; counts are descriptive, not rates.

experiment.prefix: For each of 60 seeds: build nodes 1..4 with newTestRaft(id,10,1,newTestMemoryStorage(withPeers(1,2,3))); nt := newNetwork(nodes[1],nodes[2],nodes[3]) then nt.peers[4] = nodes[4]. For 60 steps pick one of MsgHup, MsgProp, tick(), isolate, recover, TransferLeader, a ConfChangeV2 proposal on the leader (single change, target drawn from node 4 or a non-leader member, half the time JointImplicit), a restart of a random node, or persist/apply of all nodes; after each step persist/apply nodes 1..4 (skipping one node about one time in six; capturing applied_before/applying_before; applying committed conf changes under recover and, for the first three rejections, emitting invalid_change_apply with the entry operands, applied/applying before, reapplied_entry, joint_now and the decoded log_types), then evaluate the four invariants and the liveness witness, finally emitting invariant_sweep_summary.
experiment.revision_reason: Same investigation and sweep case as the previous execution, with the rejection operand extended to decode each EntryConfChangeV2's transition and change list so the rejected history's actual changes are visible. A draft-side run reported log_types='1:t0 2:t2(tr=1,1:4) 3:t0 4:t2(tr=1,0:4)', i.e. a joint-enter removal of node 4 followed by a joint-enter addition of node 4 with no leave entry between them, which is construction feedback only and is why isolated execution is requested.
